ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.claim: The affluent man’s expectation of receiving more is false, and if he opposes the Qur’an he faces a severe penalty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r1.anchor: This, it is clear, is a totally false claim.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.claim: Affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭāʾif mistook wealth for proof that they were God's favorites and expected still more; Muhammad should leave their fate to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.anchor: These verses admonish the megalomaniac leaders of Makkah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.claim: The passage describes a general wealthy, high-status mentality, not Walīd ibn Mughīrah alone, though it applies to him too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.anchor: there is no reason for restricting the verse to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r7.claim: Such favors should have made him grateful and obedient, but he became arrogant and claimed he would receive even more in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r7.anchor: The obligation of divine favours bestowed on him was that he be a grateful and obedient person to his Lord

QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r2.claim: He expects God to increase his blessings further.

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.claim: God had fully expanded the man's wealth; he still hoped for more, but God calls him obstinate toward the signs.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r1.anchor: بسطت له في المال كل البسط، ثم يطمع أن أزيد كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r1.claim: Here thumma conveys reproach and astonishment, like telling a guest who was housed and fed, “then you insult me”; Rāzī compares the incredulous turn with 6:1.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r1.anchor: لفظ ثم ههنا معناه التعجب كما تقول لصاحبك : أنزلتك داري وأطعمتك وأسقيتك ثم أنت تشتمني

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say he expected more wealth and children in this world despite having disbelieved in God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل : ثم يرجو أن أزيد في ماله وولده وقد كفر بي

RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r3.claim: Another view makes the hoped-for increase an afterlife reward: he reportedly claimed that, if Muḥammad were truthful, Paradise had been created only for him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p176#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : أن تلك الزيادة في الآخرة قيل : إنه كان يقول إن كان محمد صادقا فما خلقت الجنة

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.claim: The verses are applied specifically to al-Walīd’s great wealth, seven or ten sons, learning, and eloquence among Quraysh.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.anchor: These verses are said to refer specifically to the great fortune that God had bestowed upon al-Walīd, who was among the wealthiest men in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r7.claim: The passage can also describe the human tendency to keep wanting more, as in the well-known saying about Adam’s son wishing for a second gold valley even after receiving one.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r7.anchor: These verses can, however, also be taken in a general sense as a reference to the human tendency to want ever more

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r8.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r8.claim: A hadith says that if Adam’s son had a valley of gold, he would wish to have two.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r8.anchor: as in a well-known ḥadīth, “If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r4.claim: He hopes for further increase in wealth, sons, and arrangements; kallā rebukes him, while ʿanīd means defiant and boastful of what he has.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r4.anchor: أي ثم يطمع أن أزيد فيما جعلت له من المال والبنين ومهدت له من التمهيد

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r5.claim: An unnamed report says al-Walid’s wealth and children diminished after this verse until he died.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r5.anchor: قيل، ما زال الوليد بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله وولده حتى هلك

BURSEVI:v10p176/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r3.claim: Thumma marks distance and disapproval: hope for more is absurd after customary maximum abundance, or undeserved because he is ungrateful and defies the Benefactor.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r3.anchor: وثم استبعاد واستنكار لطمعه وحرصه إما لأنه لا مزيد على ما أوتيه سعة وكثرة

BURSEVI:v10p176/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p176/r4.claim: Bursevī also reasons that further favor will not be combined with his disbelief and ingratitude from now on.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r4.anchor: من كفران النعم ومعاندة المنعم أي لا يجمع له بعد اليوم بين الكفر

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r5.claim: Despite disbelieving and failing to thank God for these blessings, he still hopes God will increase them.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r5.anchor: لم يشكرني على هذه النعم بل كفر نعمائي وهو مع ذلك يطمع

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r6.claim: The rebuke means God will not grant the increase he expects while he remains ungrateful.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r6.anchor: لا يكون كما ظن ولا أزيده مع كفره

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, the rebuke commands him to stop and restrain himself because events will not follow his expectation.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r7.anchor: كلا معناه انزجر وارتدع فليس الأمر على ما تتوهم

THALABI:v10p71/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p71/r17.claim: Al-Walid hoped that God would increase his wealth and children.
THALABI:v10p71/r17.anchor: ثم يطمع يرجو أن أزيد مالا وولدا

THALABI:v10p71/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p71/r18.claim: Here “No!” cuts off the hope he had cherished and connects with the preceding statement.
THALABI:v10p71/r18.anchor: كلا قطع الرجاء عما كان يطمع فيه ويكون متصلا بالكلام الأول

THALABI:v10p71/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r19.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p71/r19.claim: Alternatively, “No!” is an oath meaning “truly” and begins a new verse.
THALABI:v10p71/r19.anchor: وقيل: قسم أي حقا وتكون ابتداء آية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r1.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says thumma expresses surprise and rebuke, like telling someone you housed and fed him, yet he insults you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r2.claim: This use of thumma is compared to 6:1, where it introduces the surprising disbelief of those who reject their Lord after creation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r2.anchor: وهذا كقوله عز وجل: {الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say al-Walid hopes for more wealth and children despite disbelieving in God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p422/r3.anchor: أن أزيد في ماله وولده وقد كفر بي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r5.claim: Despite these gifts, he hopes for yet more wealth and children.

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r3.claim: Al-Walid is reported to have said that if Muhammad were truthful, Paradise must have been created for him.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r3.anchor: Muhammed sâdık ise cennet benim için yaratılmış demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.claim: The passage’s general lesson is that gratitude to the giver of blessings is a basic moral duty grounded in reason and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.anchor: Nimete karşı şükretmek, nimet sahibine minnettar olmak en yalın ahlâkî ödevlerden biri, akıl ve adalet gereğidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.claim: Failing to thank God for life and material and spiritual gifts is grave ingratitude, especially when it advances denial, polytheism, and injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.anchor: varlığımızı, hayatımızı, sahip olduğumuz, yararlandığımız her türlü maddî ve mânevî nimet ve imkânları lutfeden Allah’a minnettar olmamak, şükretmemek

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r1.claim: ʿUmar instructs the judge to treat people equally in appearance, justice, and seating, so the powerful do not expect favoritism and the weak do not despair of justice.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r1.anchor: من عبد الله عمر بن الخطاب أمير المؤمنين إلى عبد الله بن قيس سلام عليك أما بعد فان القضاء فريضة محكمة وسنة متبعة فافهم

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r2.claim: The claimant bears the burden of proof and the denier swears an oath; settlement is allowed except one that makes the forbidden lawful or the lawful forbidden.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r2.anchor: البينة على من ادعى واليمين على من أنكر والصلح جائز بين المسلمين إلا صلحا أحل حراما أو حرم حلالا

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r3.claim: A judge should not let yesterday’s ruling prevent a return to the truth after reconsideration; truth is old, and revising a decision is better than persisting in error.

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r4.claim: When neither scripture nor Sunna settles a matter, understand its analogues and compare cases to identify the one most like the truth.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r4.anchor: الفهم الفهم فيما تلجلج في صدرك مما ليس في كتاب ولا سنة ثم اعرف الأشباه والأمثال

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r5.claim: Set a deadline for a claimant with an absent claim or proof; if proof arrives, enforce the right, and otherwise decide the case, which removes doubt and confusion.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r5.anchor: أمدا ينتهي إليه فان أحضر بينه أخذت له بحقه

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r6.claim: Treat Muslims as upright except one punished for a ḥadd, proven to have given false testimony, or suspect in clientage or lineage; judges decide outwardly by faith and evidence, while God knows what is hidden.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r6.anchor: المسلمون عدول بعضهم على بعض إلا مجلودا في حد أو مجربا عليه شهادة زور أو ظنينا

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r7.claim: The judge must avoid anger, impatience, annoyance with litigants, and hostility during disputes, since just decisions bring divine reward and lasting merit.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r7.anchor: وإياك والغلق والضجر والتأذي بالخصوم والتنكر عند الخصومات فان الحق في مواطن الحق يعظم الله به الأجر

BAQILLANI:v1p140/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r8.claim: A judge with sincere intentions and self-discipline will be supported by God; one who feigns qualities God knows he lacks will be disgraced, despite God’s reward and mercy.
BAQILLANI:v1p140/r8.anchor: فمن صحت نيته وأقبل على نفسه كفاه الله ما بينه وبين الناس ومن تخلق للناس بما يعلم الله

BAQILLANI:v1p241/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r1.claim: Poets have treated descriptions of horses and swords at length; a literary authority told Bāqillānī that Abu al-Hawl al-Ḥimyari’s sword poem is the best such passage.
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r1.anchor: وإن أردت أن تعرف وصاف الفرس فقد ذكرت لك أن الشعراء قد تصرفوا في ذلك بما يقع إليك

BAQILLANI:v1p241/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r2.claim: A poet should be compared with someone of the same rank, era, and standing; understanding poetic genres and quality is difficult for others but easy for trained critics.
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r2.anchor: وإنما يوازن شعر البحتري بشعر شاعر من طبقته ومن أهل عصره ومن هو في مضماره أو في منزلته ومعرفة أجناس الكلام والوقوف على أسراره

BAQILLANI:v1p241/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r3.claim: Bāqillānī prefers al-Buḥturī’s poetic surface to Ibn al-Rūmī and other contemporaries because his expression is fine, smooth, sweet, and relatively free of complexity.
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r3.anchor: نقدمه بحسن عبارته وسلاسة كلامه وعذوبة ألفاظه وقلة تعقد قوله

BAQILLANI:v1p241/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r4.claim: Poetry is attainable and within human capacity, whereas the Qur’an’s composition is beyond imagination or ambition and cannot be reached by a would-be imitator.
BAQILLANI:v1p241/r4.anchor: والشعر قبيل ملتمس مستدرك وأمر ممكن مطيع ونظم القرآن عال عن أن يعلق به الوهم أو يسمو إليه الفكر

BURHAN:v4p268/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p268/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
BURHAN:v4p268/r2.claim: Some grammarians say thumma can signal astonishment, as in the unbelievers equating their Lord and the arrogant person's hope for more.

BURHAN:v1p368/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.claim: The first class of Qur’anic كلا permits both pausing before it and beginning after it, depending on whether it is read as rebuke or confirmation; twelve examples are listed, including these four.
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.anchor: إحداها ما يجوز الوقف عليه والابتداء به

BURHAN:v1p368/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p368/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p368/r3.claim: The third class has eighteen instances where one begins with كلا but does not pause before it; the listed cases occupy fifteen suras, all in the latter half of the Qur’an.

BURHAN:v1p368/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p368/r4.speaker: عبد العزيز الديريني
BURHAN:v1p368/r4.claim: Al-Dayrini’s verse mnemonic says كلا never descended in Yathrib and never appears in the upper half of the Qur’an.
BURHAN:v1p368/r4.anchor: وللشيخ عبد العزيز الديرينى رحمه الله

BURHAN:v1p368/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p368/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p368/r5.claim: The word recurs in the latter half because most of it was revealed in Mecca, where tyrants were numerous and threats, reproaches, and denunciations were needed; the Jews in the first half were weak and humiliated.
BURHAN:v1p368/r5.anchor: وحكمة ذلك أن النصف الآخر نزل أكثره بمكة

ITQAN:v4p487/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p487/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says whoever seeks the knowledge of earlier and later generations should probe the Qur’an deeply.
ITQAN:v4p487/r1.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود من أراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليثور القرآن

ITQAN:v4p487/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p487/r2.claim: The cited claims about Qur’anic knowledge cannot be attained by relying only on surface interpretation.
ITQAN:v4p487/r2.anchor: قال وهذا الذي قالاه لا يحصل بمجرد تفسير الظاهر

ITQAN:v4p487/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p487/r3.claim: Some scholars say each verse has sixty thousand understandings; transmitted outward tafsir must first be mastered, after which inference can expand.
ITQAN:v4p487/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء لكل آية ستون ألف فهم فهذا يدل على أن في فهم معاني القرآن مجالا رحبا ومتسعا بالغا

ITQAN:v4p487/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p487/r4.claim: Claiming Qur’anic secrets without mastering apparent tafsir is like claiming to reach a house’s center without passing through its door.
ITQAN:v4p487/r4.anchor: ومن ادعى فهم أسرار القرآن ولم يحكم التفسير الظاهر فهو كمن ادعى البلوغ إلى صدر البيت قبل أن يجاوز الباب

ITQAN:v4p487/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r5.speaker: تاج الدين ابن عطاء الله
ITQAN:v4p487/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAta Allah says Sufi interpretation does not redirect the apparent sense: linguistic meaning remains, while God may open inward meanings to some hearts.
ITQAN:v4p487/r5.anchor: وقال الشيخ تاج الدين بن عطاء الله في كتابه لطائف المنن اعلم أن تفسير هذه الطائفة لكلام الله وكلام رسوله بالمعاني العربية ليس إحالة للظاهر عن ظاهره

ITQAN:v4p487/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p487/r6.speaker: تاج الدين ابن عطاء الله
ITQAN:v4p487/r6.claim: He cites “Every verse has an outward and an inward meaning” and says Sufis do not claim their inward reading is the verse’s only meaning.
ITQAN:v4p487/r6.anchor: وقد جاء في الحديث ( لكل آية ظهر وبطن ) فلا يصدنك عن تلقي هذه المعاني منهم

ITQAN:v1p235/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p235/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p235/r1.claim: Some “kallā” instances mean “indeed” and cannot be paused at; where affirmation or rebuke is possible, both pausing and continuing are allowed.
ITQAN:v1p235/r1.anchor: والباقي منها ما هو بمعنى حقا قطعا فلا يوقف عليه ومنها ما احتمل الأمرين ففيه الوجهان

ITQAN:v1p235/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p235/r2.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v1p235/r2.claim: Makkī’s first category has eleven places where pausing as rebuke is preferred, though beginning it as “indeed” is also allowed.
ITQAN:v1p235/r2.anchor: وقال مكي هي أربعة أقسام الأول ما يحسن الوقف فيه عليها على معنى الردع وهو الاختيار ويجوز الابتداء بها على معنى حقا

ITQAN:v1p235/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p235/r5.speaker: مكي
ITQAN:v1p235/r5.claim: The remaining eighteen instances are not suitable for pausing before but can begin a clause.
ITQAN:v1p235/r5.anchor: الرابع ما لا يحسن الوقف عليها ولكن يبتدأ بها وهو الثمانية عشر الباقية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r1.claim: Dhu al-Rummah’s silver touched by gold image is more readily possible, while pearls scattered on blue cloth are rarer and therefore more novel.

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r2.claim: Composite similes divide into images that cannot occur, such as ruby banners on emerald spears, and images that can occur but are rare, such as pearls on blue cloth.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r2.anchor: المقدر الذي لا يباشر الوجود نحو قوله

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r3.claim: Impossible imagined images create greater wonder than rare possible ones because nothing is farther from sight than what cannot exist; aesthetic force rises with the strength of this cause.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r3.anchor: لا مزيد في بعد الشىء عن العيون على أن يكون وجوده ممتنعا أصلا حتى لا يتصور إلا في الوهم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r4.claim: This distinction explains why similes differ in strangeness and delight, and why some produce a stronger thrill than others.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p149/r4.anchor: وفي هذا التقرير ما تعلم به الطريق إلى التشبيه من أين تفاوت في كونه غريبا

ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r5.claim: Despite these gifts, the man greedily wants God to give him still more.
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r5.anchor: he greedily desires that I give yet more

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.claim: Meccan opponents repeatedly alleged that the Quran was human fabrication, borrowed ancient lore, or material copied from earlier writings and dictated to Muhammad; the Quran records these charges and reasons against their falsehood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.anchor: ويسجل القرآن مفترياتهم لا يكتمها، ويجادلهم فيها بما يهدي كل ذي عقل وبصيرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.claim: Al-Muddaththir is the counterpart of the preceding al-Muzzammil; their central themes are essentially the same and their names share a meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes of both sūrahs .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.claim: Verses 11–17 warn that Judgment Day will be severe for disbelievers who presume their wealth and rank will bring them still more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should well inform the people about the afflictions of the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r9.claim: The man treats his possessions as an inherited entitlement and expects God to grant him even more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r9.anchor: they held that whatever they had was their right by birth and they would be blessed with even more

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.claim: At the pilgrimage season, Quraysh ask al-Walid for a single story about Muhammad; after rejecting soothsayer, madman, poet, and sorcerer as accurate descriptions, he recommends calling him a sorcerer because people see him as dividing families.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.anchor: ثم إن الوليد بن المغيرة اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش، وكان ذا سن فيهم، وقد حضر الموسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r4.claim: His desire is for further increase beyond the wealth and children already given him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r4.anchor: أي على ما أعطيته من المال والولد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the hope as incredulous rebuke: after such abundance, there is no more to add; كلا cuts off and restrains his hope.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329/r6.anchor: قال الزمخشري: استبعاد لطمعه واستنكار، أي لا مزيد على ما أوتي كثرة وسعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r1.claim: He still expects more than what he has been given; the expectation is absurd either because his wealth is already ample or because it accompanies ingratitude and defiance.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r1.anchor: على ما أديته وهو استبعاد واستنكار لطمعه وحرصه إما لأنه في غنى تام لا مزيد على ما أوتي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others report that al-Walīd said that, if Muḥammad were truthful, paradise had been created for him alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن وغيره أنه كان يقول إن كان محمد صادقا فما خلقت الجنة إلا لي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r3.claim: “Thumma” commonly marks remoteness or improbability here: the moral distance is represented as temporal distance, as in expecting kindness after mistreating someone.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r3.anchor: وكان ذلك لتنزيل البعد المعنوي منزلة البعد الزماني

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r4.claim: Some call this a shift in rank, but al-Ālūsī says that is not apt; the point is the absurd distance between the conduct and the expectation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#4/r4.anchor: قيل التفات الرتبي بل عد الشيء بعيدا غير مناسب لما عطف عليه كما تقول تسيء إلي ثم ترجو إحساني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r1.claim: The outward meaning must be mastered before seeking the inward: claiming esoteric understanding before mastering exoteric tafsir is like claiming to reach the room's front before entering through its door.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r1.anchor: وقالوا لا بد منه أولا إذ لا يطمع في الوصول إلى الباطن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r2.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran has many subjects and layers, inexhaustible wonders, and outward recitation with inward interpretation; one who approaches it gently is saved, while one who approaches violently falls.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r2.anchor: عن إبن عباس قال : القرآن ذو شجون وفنون وظهور وبطون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r3.speaker: إبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says that whoever seeks knowledge of the earliest and latest peoples should read the Quran; al-Alusi notes that this exceeds what outward exegesis alone provides.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r3.anchor: وقال إبن مسعود : من أراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليتل القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r4.claim: An unnamed trusted authority says each verse has sixty thousand understandings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r4.anchor: وقد قال بعض من يوثق به لكل آية ستون ألف فهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r5.claim: Al-Hasan transmits a Prophetic report that every verse has an outward and inward meaning, every letter a limit, and every limit an access point.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لكل آية ظهر وبطن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r6.speaker: إبن النقيب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r6.claim: Ibn al-Naqib defines the outward as meanings apparent to scholars of exoteric learning and the inward as secrets God discloses to people of spiritual realities.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r6.anchor: قال إبن النقيب أن ظاهرها ما ظهر من معانيها لأهل العلم بالظاهر وباطنها ما تضمنته

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r7.speaker: إبن النقيب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r7.claim: For Ibn al-Naqib, a letter's limit marks the endpoint of its intended meaning, while its access point is a means of reaching enough knowledge of an obscure meaning or ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r7.anchor: ومعنى قوله ولكل حرف حد أن لكل حرف منتهي فيما أراده الله تعالى من معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r8.claim: Another transmitted wording says each verse has an outward, inward, limit, and access point.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r8.anchor: وقيل في رواية لكل آية ظهر وبطن وحد ومطلع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r9.claim: The outward is the wording and its conventional and signaled meanings used as routes to derive the five legal rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r9.anchor: والمذكور بوساطة الألفاظ وتأليفاتها وضعا وإفادة وجعلها طرقا إلى إستنباط الأحكام الخمسة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r10.claim: The inward is the spirit of the words: divine speech apprehended beyond the faculties of ordinary discursive instruments through sanctified spiritual perception.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r10.anchor: وروح الألفاظ أعنى الكلام المعتلى عن المدارك الآلية بجواهر الروح القدسية هو البطن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r11.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r11.claim: Al-Sadiq's saying that God has manifested Himself to His servants in His Book, though they do not see, points to the access point as ascent from inward speech to the divine Speaker's Name.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r11.anchor: بقول الصادق لقد تجلى الله تعالى في كتابه لعباده ولكن لا يبصرون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r12.claim: One mystical account places the limit between outward and inward or between inward and access point; the latter ascent recognizes the relation of attribute to Name and the servant's attribute's effacement under divine theophany.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r12.anchor: وإستهلاك صفة العبد تحت تجليات أنوار صفة المتكلم تعالى شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r13.claim: A further view calls the outward tafsir, the inward ta'wil, the limit the reach of human understanding, and the access point the ascent from that reach to witnessing God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p7/r13.anchor: وقيل الظهر التفسير والبطن التأويل والحد ما تتناهى إليه الفهوم من معنى الكلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r5.claim: He hopes that God will increase his wealth, children, and comfort.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r5.anchor: {ثم يطمع} يرجو {أن أزيد} أي أن أزيده مالا وولدا وتمهيدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r6.claim: Kallā rejects the hope: God will not grant him further increase.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r6.anchor: {كلا} لا أفعل ولا أزيده، قالوا: فما زال الوليد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r7.claim: It is said that after the verse was revealed, al-Walid's wealth and children kept declining until his death.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r7.anchor: قالوا: فما زال الوليد بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله وولده حتى هلك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r2.claim: His hope for further increase is far-fetched either because he has already received all that can be given or because his ingratitude and defiance make him undeserving.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:14-17/r2.anchor: وهو استبعاد لطمعه أما لأنه لا مزيد على ما أوتي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r3.claim: Thumma marks the shocking distance between God’s immense favors and al-Walid’s later denial, after which he still expects an increase.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r3.anchor: مشيرا بأداة التراخي إلى استبعاد الزيادة له على حالته هذه من عدم الشكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r4.claim: He expects further worldly or afterlife favor without offering gratitude, even while he denies God’s messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p225/r4.anchor: أزيد * } أي فيما آتيته من دنياه أو آخرته وهو يكذب رسولي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r6.claim: Mujahid says al-Walid kept seeing his wealth and children decline until he died.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r11.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r11.claim: Abu Malik says no child was born to al-Walid after that point and his wealth did not increase beyond what he already had.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r11.anchor: عن أبي مالك {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r6.claim: Mujahid says he kept seeing his wealth and children decline until he perished.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r6.anchor: ثم يطمع ان ازيد كلا قال : فما زال يرى النقصان في ماله وولده حتى هلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r1.claim: Thumma marks a higher degree: more astonishing still, al-Walid expects his blessings to increase; the expectation is unlikely, as kallā makes explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r1.anchor: و { ثم } في قوله : { ثم يطمع } للتراخي الرتبي ، أي وأعظم من ذلك أنه يطمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r2.anchor: والطمع : طلب الشيء العظيم وجعل متعلق طمعه زيادة مما جعل الله له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r3.claim: The attribution of increase to God either reflects that idolaters did not ascribe provision to idols, or reminds al-Walid that God gave the blessing he seeks to enlarge while forgetting its giver.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r3.anchor: لأنهم لم يكونوا يسندون الرزق إلى الأصنام ، أو لأنه طمع في زيادة النعمة غير متذكر أنها من عند الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r4.claim: The wording ‘that I increase’ is chosen instead of ‘he hopes for an increase’ or ‘he hopes to be increased’ to make that reminder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r4.anchor: ولهذه النكتة عدل عن أن يقال : يطمع في الزيادة ، أو يطمع أن يزاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r5.claim: Kallā rebukes and cancels his expectation of further blessings, cutting off his hope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r5.anchor: وكلا } ردع وإبطال لطمعه في الزيادة من النعم وقطع لرجائه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r6.claim: The warning tells al-Walid his provision will be cut and reassures the Prophet, lest opponents take prosperity as proof that defiance is harmless and there is no afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r6.anchor: والمقصود إبلاغ هذا إليه مع تطمين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن الوليد سيقطع عنه مدد الرزق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r7.claim: The feared misuse of worldly wealth recalls Moses' prayer that Pharaoh's wealth be erased because it led people astray.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r7.anchor: كما حكى الله من قول موسى عليه السلام : { ربنا إنك آتيت فرعون وملأه زينة وأموالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r8.claim: The rebuke signals that ingratitude brings blessings to an end, as 14:7 states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r8.anchor: وفي هذا الإبطال والردع إيذان بأن كفران النعمة سبب لقطعها قال تعالى : { لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r9.speaker: الشيخ ابن عطاء الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ Allāh says ingratitude exposes blessings to loss, while gratitude binds them fast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r9.anchor: ولهذا قال الشيخ ابن عطاء الله : ( من لم يشكر النعم فقد تعرض لزوالها ، ومن شكرها فقد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.claim: The following statement about stubbornness toward God's signs may explain the rebuke: his ingratitude became active opposition, warranting removal of blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r10.anchor: يجوز أن تكون هذه الجملة تعليلا للردع والإبطال ، أي لأن شدة معاندته لآياتنا كانت كفرانا للنعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.speaker: الماتريدي والمعتزلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.claim: Al-Maturidi and the Muʿtazilites hold that an unbeliever may receive God's favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r11.anchor: فإن الكافر يكون منعما عليه على المختار وهو قول الماتريدي والمعتزلة خلافا للأشعري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.speaker: الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.claim: Al-Ashʿari differs, denying that an unbeliever receives God's favor in this sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r12.anchor: وهو قول الماتريدي والمعتزلة خلافا للأشعري ، واختار المحققون أنه خلاف لفظي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p305/r13.claim: The author follows the careful scholars who regard the disagreement over God's favor to unbelievers as verbal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r15.claim: The verse describes al-Walid and Utba's greed for further worldly increase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r15.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ثم يطمع أن أزيد وصفه بجشع الوليد وعتبة في الازدياد من الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r1.claim: He hopes that God will admit him to Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما يطمع أن أدخله الجنة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, he hopes for an increase in wealth and children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أن أزيده من المال والولد قاله مقاتل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.claim: Despite all these blessings, he still hoped for more; his hostility means that, knowingly, he disbelieved in response to God’s favors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#3/r2.anchor: أي: معاندا، وهو الكفر على نعمه بعد العلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r2.claim: Kallā rebukes and means desist, like ṣah for silence and mah for stopping; alternatively it means “indeed.”
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r2.anchor: و (كلا): ردع وزجر، كأنه قيل: ارتدع عن هذا وانزجر، كما أن (صه) بمنزلة اسكت،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.claim: Abundant blessings make disobedience toward the Benefactor more serious.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على أن كثرة النعم توجب عظم عصيان المنعم.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.claim: An increase in blessings can become a source of corruption.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن مزيد النعم قد يكون مفسدة لذلك قال: (ثم يطمع أن أزيد (15) كلا إنه كان لآياتنا عنيدا (16).

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitability is shown by enemies’ failure to meet the challenge despite intense opposition; they resort to insults and fighting instead of rebuttal.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r5.anchor: وتدل على إعجاز القرآن؛ لأنهم مع شدة عداوتهم لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -،

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.claim: Calling unbelief an attempt to invalidate truth bad supports Abu Hashim’s view that reflection can be bad, against Abu Ali.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن الكفر لإبطال الحق يقبح، فتدل على قول أبي هاشم: إن في النظر ما يقبح، خلاف قول أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.claim: Thinking and grimacing are acts performed by the human servant.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r7.anchor: وتدل أن الفكر والعبوس فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r20.claim: The phrase incredulously condemns his greed: after such abundance, he expects still more.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r21.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r21.claim: It is said he claimed Paradise had been created only for him if Muhammad was truthful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r21.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان يقول : إن كان محمد صادقا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r26.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r26.claim: Al-Hasan says he hoped for admission to Paradise, but the verse answers no.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r26.anchor: أحدهما : ثم يطمع أن أدخله الجنة , كلا , قاله الحسن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r27.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r27.claim: Ibn Abbas says he hoped for more wealth and children; thereafter they kept diminishing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r27.anchor: الثاني : أن أزيده من المال والولد ( كلا ) قال ابن عباس : فلم يزل النقصان في ماله وولده .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r28.claim: A further possibility is that he hoped God would support him despite his unbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r28.anchor: ويحتمل وجها ثالثا : ثم يطمع أن أنصره على كفره .

MUQATIL:74:11-17/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r5.claim: Al-Walid hoped for more, but God would cut off his provision and destroy him; he became impoverished, begged, and died poor among those marked for destruction.
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r5.anchor: لا أزيده بل أقطع ذلك عنه وأهلكه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r1.claim: The wording expresses disapproval and astonishment at his greed: he hopes for more wealth and children without gratitude.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r1.anchor: استبعاد واستنكار لطمعه وحرصه فيرجو أن أزيد في ماله وولده من غير شكر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says he hoped for entry to Paradise and wealth and children there, as in his boast that he would be given wealth and offspring.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#4/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن أن أزيد أن أدخله الجنة فاوتيه مالا وولدا كما قال لأوتين مالا وولدا

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r5.claim: After all those gifts, al-Walid hoped God would increase his wealth and children.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r5.anchor: أي ثم إن الوليد يطمع بعد هذا كله أن أزيده في المال والولد

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r7.claim: Hasan and others say al-Walid hoped to enter Paradise, claiming that if Muhammad were truthful Paradise was created for him; God rejects this.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن وغيره: أي ثم يطمع أن أدخله الجنة، وكان الوليد يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r9.claim: Thumma is exclamatory, not sequential, expressing astonishment; Qurtubi links it to 6:1 and an analogy of giving much only to be treated harshly.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r9.anchor: و «ثم» في قوله تعالى: { ثم يطمع } ليست بثم التي للنسق ولكنها تعجيب

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r10.claim: Another view says al-Walid hoped provision would remain among his descendants, thinking Muhammad’s memory would end at his death.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r10.anchor: وقيل يطمع أن أترك ذلك في عقبه وذلك أنه كان يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r11.claim: A further interpretation says al-Walid hoped God would support him despite disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:14-16/r11.anchor: وقيل: أي ثم يطمع أن أنصره على كفره
